narr: An upper low parked over the Mid-South resulted in widespread showers and thunderstorms across North Mississippi during the early morning hours of June 8, 2021. Some locations received up to 4 inches of rain before sunrise which set the stage for flash flooding later that morning into the afternoon as a mesoscale convective vortex pushed into the Mid-South. This feature resulted in several areas of showers and thunderstorms moving across North Mississippi during the day with numerous reports of flash flooding and 24-hour rainfall totals of more than 6 inches. During the afternoon enough surface-based instability developed to support a few severe storms with damaging winds and a weak tornado.
ev: There was widespread flooding in the Tutwiler area. There were eight inches of water in at least two homes on West Street.
County Road 7 and County Road 299 were flooded with more than 6 inches of flowing water.
Several low-lying roads were flooded in northwest Quitman County.
County Road 102 was closed due to flash flooding.

Several cars were stalled in floodwaters due to street flooding in Batesville. Part of Old Panola Road was washed out near the bridge over the Tallahatchie River. In total, 23 roads were impacted across Panola County.
Portions of County Roads 102 and 104 were closed due to flash flooding.

A creek running under County Road 224 east of Water Valley eroded the ground under the road. The roadbed was left intact. A vehicle drove over the compromised road, causing the roadbed to collapse. The vehicle fell into the creek and the driver had to be pulled out. Several mobile homes were flooded along Oklahoma Street in Coffeeville. There was significant flooding on Central Street in Water Valley. In total, six homes and three roads were impacted.
Several cars were stalled in floodwaters due to significant street flooding in Charleston.
Several cars were stalled in floodwaters in downtown New Albany. Water was several feet deep in some locations, including Main Street.
Numerous roads were blocked due to significant flooding across Lafayette County. County Road 381 was closed and there was flooding in the Oaks Subdivision just north of Oxford.
